testCase.question: A restaurant proposes a sidewalk café with furniture near a building exit and cellar hatch. The owner says outdoor-dining authorization allows the exterior seats to be counted separately from the interior PACO and eliminates further accessibility review. The documents do not say whether the café is beyond the building line, enclosed, or separated from the interior seating by a Section 713 fire partition. What can be concluded from the selected Building Code passages, and what remains unresolved?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The proposal cannot be approved from the selected evidence. If it is a sidewalk café beyond the building line, BC 3111.1 requires compliance not only with Section 3111 but also with Chapter 32 and separate zoning and agency requirements; the selected evidence does not provide those outside rules. BC 3111.4 prohibits café components from obstructing a building exit or cellar hatch. Its cellar-entrance exception is not automatic: it requires a special application, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and a cellar entrance or areaway that is not required egress. BC 3111.6 makes Chapter 11 applicable to the café and its access. BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with not less than one accessible space at each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed and located on a level served by an accessible route. BC 3111.7 supplies only a conditional rule for an enclosed sidewalk café: unless a Section 713 fire partition separates it from inside seating, its seating is added to the inside seating solely to determine whether a PACO is required. These passages do not establish the approved interior capacity, the treatment of every open exterior seating arrangement, property-line or operational jurisdiction, current agency authorization, or overall approval.

expectedUncertainty.description: The selected passages establish several conditional Building Code constraints, but they do not establish overall approval, current agency jurisdiction, or lawful seating capacity.

answer.answerText:
The owner’s claim is not supported by the selected passages. Outdoor-dining authorization does not, on this evidence, eliminate Building Code accessibility review: sidewalk cafés and access to them must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces must be accessible, with at least one accessible space of each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

If the proposed café is beyond the building line, it must also comply with BC 3111, the Zoning Resolution, applicable Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioner requirements, and Chapter 32 projection limits. The asserted authorization is not evidence here that those separate requirements have been met.

Café awnings, enclosures, fixtures, equipment, and removable platforms may not obstruct a building exit, cellar access hatch, or areaway. Proximity to an exit or hatch does not alone prove an obstruction, so the proposed layout cannot be found compliant or noncompliant without the relevant geometry. A platform may cover a cellar entrance or areaway only if, upon special application, the commissioner permits an easily removable, prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and the entrance or areaway is not used as a required means of egress.

Separate exterior seating counting for PACO purposes is not established merely by outdoor-dining authorization. For an enclosed sidewalk café, its seating must be added to interior seating to determine whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, unless it is separated from the interior seating by fire partitions complying with Section 713. Because enclosure status, seating counts, and the asserted fire-partition compliance are unknown, the selected passages do not establish the final PACO result or its threshold.

Material unresolved items are the building/property-line location; enclosure status; interior and exterior seating counts; Section 713 fire-partition status; exit and cellar-hatch/areaway geometry; whether the cellar access is a required means of egress; dining-surface types, total seating and standing spaces, accessible-space distribution, and accessible-route/level conditions; and the current agency authorization records. If a hatch-cover platform is proposed, its special application, commissioner permission, removability, designation, and Section 3111.5 design basis are also unresolved.
answer.conclusion: The owner’s claim is not supported by the selected passages. Outdoor-dining authorization does not, on this evidence, eliminate Building Code accessibility review: sidewalk cafés and access to them must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces must be accessible, with at least one accessible space of each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

supportedPoints.explanation: A sidewalk café provided beyond the building line must comply with BC 3111, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the requirements of the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and Chapter 32 projection limitations.

supportedPoints.heading: Café components may not obstruct exits or cellar access
supportedPoints.explanation: No awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment, or removable platform of a sidewalk café may be located so as to obstruct a building exit or a cellar access hatch or areaway. Upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5 to cover a cellar entrance or areaway only when it is not used as a required means of egress.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessibility applies to the café and its access
supportedPoints.explanation: Sidewalk cafés and access to them must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces for consuming food or drink are provided, accessible seating and standing spaces must equal at least 10 percent of the total number, with not fewer than one accessible space of each dining-surface type. The accessible spaces must be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

supportedPoints.heading: Enclosed sidewalk-café seating generally combines with interior seating
supportedPoints.explanation: For an enclosed sidewalk café, seating must be added to seating inside the building to determine whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, unless the café seating is separated from interior seating by fire partitions complying with Section 713.
